arxiv-1810-01140.title: Training compact deep learning models for video classification using circulant matrices
arxiv-1810-01140.creator: Alexandre Araujo, Benjamin Negrevergne, Yann Chevaleyre, Jamal Atif
arxiv-1810-01140.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Alexandre Araujo, Benjamin Negrevergne, Yann Chevaleyre, Jamal Atif. In real world scenarios, model accuracy is hardly the only factor to consider. Large models consume more memory and are computationally more intensive, which makes them difficult to train and to deploy, especially on mobile devices. In this paper, we build on recent results at the crossroads of Linear Algebra and Deep Learning which demonstrate how imposing a structure on large weight matrices can be used to reduce the size of the model.

arxiv-2012-09712.title: Deep Molecular Dreaming: Inverse machine learning for de-novo molecular design and interpretability with surjective representations
arxiv-2012-09712.creator: Cynthia Shen cynt.shen@mail.utoronto.ca, Mario Krennmario.krenn@utoronto.ca, Sagi Eppelsagieppel@gmail.com, Alán Aspuru-Guzikalan@aspuru.com
arxiv-2012-09712.description: Abstract Computer-based de-novo design of functional molecules is one of the most prominent challenges in cheminformatics today. As a result, generative and evolutionary inverse designs from the field of artificial intelligence have emerged at a rapid pace, with aims to optimize molecules for a particular chemical property.

arxiv-2305-01948.description: Abstract An acyclic edge coloring of a graph is a proper edge coloring without any bichromatic cycles. The acyclic chromatic index of a graph G G denoted by a ′ ​ ( G ) a^{\prime}(G) , is the minimum k k such that G G has an acyclic edge coloring with k k colors.

arxiv-2601-09646.title: Long-Term Average Impulse and Singular Control of a Growth Model with Two Revenue Sources Thanks: This research was supported by the Simons Foundation under grant number 8035009.
arxiv-2601-09646.creator: K.L. Helmes, R.H. Stockbridge, C. Zhu
arxiv-2601-09646.description: Abstract This paper analyzes and explicitly solves a class of long-term average impulse control problems and a related class of singular control problems. The underlying process is a general one-dimensional diffusion with appropriate boundary behavior. The model is motivated by applications such as the optimal long-term management of renewable resources and financial portfolio management.

pmc-10613231.title: Loss of adenosine A3 receptors accelerates skeletal muscle regeneration in mice following cardiotoxin-induced injury
pmc-10613231.creator: Nastaran Tarban, Albert Bálint Papp, Dávid Deák, Péter Szentesi, Hajnalka Halász, Andreas Patsalos, László Csernoch, Zsolt Sarang, Zsuzsa Szondy
pmc-10613231.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Skeletal muscle regeneration is a complex process orchestrated by multiple interacting steps. An increasing number of reports indicate that inflammatory responses play a central role in linking initial muscle injury responses to timely muscle regeneration following injury. The nucleoside adenosine has been known for a long time as an endogenously produced anti-inflammatory molecule that is generated in high amounts during tissue injury. It mediates its physiological effects via four types of adenosine receptors.

pmc-11366729.title: Perceptual comparisons induce lasting and generalizing changes to face memory reports
pmc-11366729.creator: Jerrick Teoh, Joseph M. Saito, Yvanna Yeo, Sophia Winter, Keisuke Fukuda
pmc-11366729.description: Humans are often tasked to remember new faces so that they can recognize the faces later in time. Previous studies found that memory reports for basic visual features (e.g., colors and shapes) are susceptible to systematic distortions as a result of comparison with new visual input, especially when the input is perceived as similar to the memory.

pmc-11507142.title: QTL Mapping-Based Identification of Visceral White-Nodules Disease Resistance Genes in Larimichthys polyactis
pmc-11507142.creator: Qian Li, Jiajie Zhu, Sifang Liu, Haowen Liu, Tianle Zhang, Ting Ye, Bao Lou, Feng Liu
pmc-11507142.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Disease outbreaks in aquaculture have recently intensified. In particular, visceral white-nodules disease, caused by Pseudomonas plecoglossicida, has severely hindered the small yellow croaker (Larimichthys polyactis) aquaculture industry. However, research on this disease is limited. To address this gap, the present study employed a 100K SNP chip to genotype individuals from an F1 full-sib family, identify single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), and construct a genetic linkage map for this species.

pmc-11609178.title: Reprogrammed lipid metabolism in advanced resistant cancers: an upcoming therapeutic opportunity
pmc-11609178.creator: Mario Cioce, Mariamena Arbitrio, Nicoletta Polerà, Emanuela Altomare, Antonia Rizzuto, Carmela De Marco, Vito Michele Fazio, Giuseppe Viglietto, Maria Lucibello
pmc-11609178.description: Resistance of cancer to therapy is the main challenge to its therapeutic management and is still an unsolved problem. Rearranged lipid metabolism is a strategy adopted by cancer cells to counteract adversity during their evolution toward aggressiveness and immune evasion.

pmc-12563536.title: A Novel Allosteric Inhibitor Targeting IMPDH at Y233 Overcomes Resistance to Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors in Lymphoma
pmc-12563536.creator: Nagarajan Pattabiraman, Cosimo Lobello, David Rushmore, Luca Mologni, Mariusz Wasik, Johnvesly Basappa, Ada Funaro, Tadeusz Robak
pmc-12563536.description: Simple SummaryCancer cells often rely on altered metabolism to support their rapid growth. We discovered that two cancer-driving proteins, ALK and SRC, directly modify and activate a key metabolic enzyme called IMPDH2. This modification occurs at a specific site (Y233) and boosts the enzyme’s activity, helping cancer cells make the building blocks of DNA.

pmc-12644772.title: Differences in the risk association of TERT rs2736098 (C > T) with lung cancer between Caucasian and Asian populations: A meta-analysis
pmc-12644772.creator: Xiaozheng Wu, Wen Li, Ran Ding, Hongguan Jiao, Yihui Chai, Yunzhi Chen
pmc-12644772.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The T allele variant of TERT rs2736098 has been associated with an increased risk of lung cancer (LC), yet various studies have yielded inconsistent findings. The purpose of this study is to verify the association between the rs2736098 variant and LC risk, as well as to investigate the differences in this association across different ethnic groups (Caucasians and Asians), various LC subtypes, and distinct smoking statuses.

pmc-13459405.title: Cephalomedullary nailing of trochanteric fractures in geriatric patients restores natural hip geometry - a retrospective radiological analysis
pmc-13459405.creator: Philippe Siegenthaler, Manuel Waltenspül, Cléa Nüesch, Marie-Garance Meuwly, Michael Dietrich, Method Kabelitz
pmc-13459405.description: BackgroundTrochanteric fractures are common in geriatric patients, and cephalomedullary nailing is widely used.
